title: Change of rings of a universally tensor-acyclic complex
statement: Let O → O' be a morphism φ of commutative ring sheaves on a site with the sheafification hypotheses of lem-pur-change-of-rings-acyclic-kflat. Let E be an additive functor whose objects and maps are changeOfRings φ and changeOfRingsHom φ via equalities h and hm with equality transports. Let K be a cochain complex of O-modules such that Tot(F ⊗_O K) is acyclic for every cochain complex F of O-modules. Then termwise E(K) is acyclic as a complex of O'-modules. No K-flatness or acyclicity hypothesis on K is part of this comparison theorem.

proof.text: Let S be O' viewed as an O-module by restriction of scalars, and apply the universal tensor-acyclicity hypothesis to the single complex S[0]. All summands of degree n except S ⊗ K^n vanish, and the remaining differential is id_S ⊗ d_K. Sheafification of sectionwise tensor products identifies this complex with the restriction of termwise extension of scalars; naturality holds for every differential. Restriction of scalars has the same underlying abelian sheaf, is exact and faithful, and thus reflects acyclicity. The h and hm equalities give a natural isomorphism from E to extension of scalars, including all equality transports. Applying it termwise gives the claimed acyclicity. This argument also works for the zero ring and zero modules, and does not use flatness of the scalar extension.
